sum: American Tower raised its full-year 2026 outlook for the third time this year after reporting third-quarter results on October 27. The company cited steady leasing demand across its global tower portfolio and continued outperformance at CoreSite, its data center platform, in the American Tower financial release.

Third-quarter total revenue rose 2.5 percent to 2.785 billion US dollars, while property revenue increased 4.5 percent to 2.734 billion US dollars. Data center cash revenue grew 16.3 percent, helping offset softer trends in parts of the tower portfolio.

American Tower lifted the midpoint of its 2026 property revenue outlook by 55 million US dollars to a range of 10.785 billion to 10.865 billion US dollars. The midpoint implies 5.0 percent growth from the prior year. The Data Centers segment is expected to contribute 1.218 billion to 1.228 billion US dollars of property revenue, representing midpoint growth of 16.1 percent.

Management kept the adjusted EBITDA outlook midpoint unchanged at 7.275 billion US dollars. It lowered the net income outlook midpoint by 30 million US dollars, primarily because of unrealized losses on equity securities, while lifting the midpoint of AFFO attributable to common stockholders per share by 0.02 US dollars to a range of 11.04 to 11.16 US dollars.

Net income fell 14.4 percent to 781 million US dollars, and net income attributable to common stockholders declined 10.3 percent to 766 million US dollars. The company said the comparison was affected by unrealized losses on equity investments, which contrasted with unrealized gains in the prior-year quarter.

Why Is Tower REIT American Tower (NYSE:AMT) Drawing Attention Today?
sum: - Rising mobile-data traffic keeps communications-tower leasing central to the infrastructure conversation.
- A global footprint of macro sites spreads demand across many markets and tenant relationships.
- Connected data-center assets widen the reach of the enterprise into digital infrastructure.

American Tower (NYSE:AMT) Real Estate American Tower Corp (NYSE:AMT) 188.30 USD 0.000 0.000% Last Updated at: 2026-11-02T21:00:00Z moved into sharper focus today as rising mobile-data demand kept communications-tower leasing central to the infrastructure conversation across a market trading near record territory. The company owns and operates a vast estate of macro cell sites that carry the wireless signals underpinning everyday connectivity, and that estate has become more valuable as data traffic across the United States and abroad keeps building week after week. The name continues to stand out within the Infrastructure and Real Estate space.

The appeal of a large tower real estate enterprise rests on a simple structural trait: wireless carriers lease space on the same physical sites again and again as networks densify, and each added tenant or equipment amendment lifts the revenue a tower can generate without a matching jump in operating cost. That characteristic has kept the name in steady view even as the earnings-heavy week pulls headlines toward megacap technology and chip makers.

The draw toward the communications-tower enterprise rests on the relentless growth of mobile-data traffic. The stock is a constituent of the S&P 500, NYSE Composite and Russell 1000, which keeps it within the reach of index-tracking funds. Every new smartphone generation, every streaming habit, and every connected device adds to the signal that must travel across the network, and carriers meet that demand by adding equipment to existing towers and by leasing space on new ones. Each of those steps flows back to the owner of the physical site.

A macro tower can host several tenants at once, stacking antennas and radios from competing carriers on the same steel structure. As networks move toward denser, higher-capacity configurations, the equipment on each site tends to grow, and the leasing arrangements that govern that equipment carry built-in escalators that lift revenue over time.

items.t: American Tower Jumps 6.6% Amid Sector-Wide Rally
sum: American Tower Corporation surged 6.6% on Friday, riding a powerful rally across cell tower REITs that sent sector peers sharply higher. Shares closed at $193.59 on volume of 2.8M as the tower infrastructure sector posted its strongest collective move in months, with Crown Castle jumping 12.4% and SBA Communications climbing 8.0%.

The synchronized move reflects broad sector momentum. Crown Castle’s 12.4% gain led the group, followed by SBA Communications’ 8.0% advance and American Tower’s 6.6% rise. The coordinated surge across all three major tower REITs suggests investors are reassessing the sector rather than reacting to company-specific developments. These broad-based rallies often signal shifting expectations around wireless carrier spending, interest rate trajectories, or infrastructure investment themes that benefit the entire cell tower business model.

The rally comes despite recent analyst caution. Over the past week, American Tower saw one analyst price target cut with no offsetting target raises, indicating Friday’s move was driven by sector rotation and peer momentum rather than fresh Wall Street upgrades. The $90.2 billion market cap REIT is navigating a mixed sentiment environment, making the strength of the sector-wide rally all the more notable.

Volume and volatility accompanied the move. The 2.8M shares traded Friday reflected heightened investor interest as the stock broke out alongside its tower REIT peers. When sector peers move in lockstep with this kind of magnitude—particularly when the leader posts double-digit gains—it often indicates institutional repositioning or a catalyst affecting the entire tower infrastructure investment thesis.

SpaceX Reportedly Eyes 80,000 Cell Sites In Push To Become Fourth US Wireless Carrier: T, TMUS, VZ Stocks Slip After-Hours
sum: - AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile shares moved 4-5% lower in extended trading on the competitive implications.
- Shares of tower operators, including CCI and AMT, gained on the report.

- The potential agreements would strengthen SpaceX’s effort to establish itself as a standalone wireless competitor to the existing dominant providers, the people familiar with the discussions told Bloomberg.

Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) rose 1.4% after hours on Thursday following reports that it is pursuing agreements for a minimum of 80,000 cell sites across the United States as it advances plans to build a fourth nationwide wireless carrier.

The rocket and satellite company is in discussions with at least one major cellular infrastructure company, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Crown Castle Inc. (CCI), among the largest U.S. owners of cellular towers alongside American Tower (AMT) and Vertical Bridge, was also approached for the purpose, the report said.

SpaceX recently acquired low-band spectrum that will help integrate its Starlink satellites into what Musk has described as a “major mobile carrier.” It also received Federal Communications Commission approval to launch 15,000 satellites designed to provide mobile service directly to phones.

“We will be building out our terrestrial networks so there’s broad-based connectivity anywhere that SpaceX and Starlink are allowed to operate,” Musk said during the company’s earnings call this week. He added that satellite launches combined with the spectrum acquisition “will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US.”

US Telecom: SpaceX Mobile Comments Should Be Taken With a Grain of Salt
sum: Shares of US wireless carriers and tower firms traded lower after SpaceX SPCX claimed it will use satellite dishes to build a wireless network capable of competing in the US wireless industry. The company also claimed it will launch 10 times as many V3 broadband satellites as V2.

Why it matters: SpaceX’s potential impact on telecom is a key factor in valuations across the industry. We don’t believe the firm’s comments this quarter change the range of potential outcomes for the industry relative to our prior expectations.

- Several firms have attempted to build hotspot-type wireless networks like the one SpaceX is contemplating. The cable companies have incorporated public hotspots in tens of millions of broadband modems over the past decade, but these networks still deliver fundamentally limited signal coverage.

- We view SpaceX’s comments as part of its battle with the US wireless carriers for network access rather than a credible threat. To fill areas satellites don’t reach well without this access, SpaceX would likely need to build and manage a massive number of sites, just to attack a market that is well served today and not growing rapidly.
The bottom line: We maintain our fair value estimates and moat ratings for the US telecom and tower firms.

- Both wireless and broadband markets benefit from efficient scale attributes, but this moat source is most at risk in broadband. We recently cut our Comcast CMCSA and Charter Communications CHTR valuations, in part to reflect incremental Starlink competition. We don’t expect Starlink to threaten the wireless operations of T-Mobile TMUS, Verizon VZ, or AT&T T for the foreseeable future.

- For US tower firms American Tower AMT, Crown Castle CCI, and SBA SBAC, we believe SpaceX offers more upside potential than downside risk. We don’t factor upside from a SpaceX network buildout into our valuations, but the company would likely need tower sites to provide reliable signal coverage if it chooses to enter the wireless market.

Are Options Traders Betting on a Big Move in American Airlines Stock?
sum: Investors in American Airlines Group Inc. AAL need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the September 18, 2026 $01.00 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for American Airlines, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently,American Airlines is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Transportation - Airline Industry that ranks in the Bottom 39% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, three analysts have increased their earnings estimate for the current quarter, while three have dropped their estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter to move from a loss of nine cents per share to a loss of five cents per share in the same time period.

Given the way analysts feel aboutAmerican Airlines right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

Morgan Stanley Cuts Price Target on Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH). Here is Why
sum: With an annual dividend yield of 3.37%, Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation (NASDAQ:CTSH) is included among the 12 Best NASDAQ Stocks to Buy for Dividends.

On June 23, Morgan Stanley cut its price target on Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation (NASDAQ:CTSH) from $63 to $44, but reaffirmed its 'Equal Weight' rating on the shares. The lowered target still implies an upside of almost 4% from the current price level.

Morgan Stanley believes that demand trends are "stable-to-slightly worse", especially when it comes to securing larger managed services deals. According to the firm, the lack of any demand acceleration through mid-June raises concerns about the market's expectations for a strong second half of the year, creating potential downside risks to the current Wall Street forecasts.

On the other hand, Wedbush analyst Steven Wahrhaftig turned bullish on Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation (NASDAQ:CTSH) earlier on June 8, upgrading the stock from 'Neutral' to 'Outperform' and lifting its price objective by $14 (read more details here).
Pzena Investment Management stated the following regarding Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation (NASDAQ:CTSH) in its Q1 2026 investor letter:

"The health care, financials, and technology sectors were the largest detractors from performance during the quarter. Leading IT services provider Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation (NASDAQ:CTSH) was weak, despite reporting robust 4Q earnings with peer leading organic growth, due to fears around AI disruption to the services industry more broadly. We continue to see these fears as overblown and added to our position on weakness."

While we acknowledge the potential of CTSH as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk.
